questions.question: Intensive agriculture implies ______.

options.text: cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labour and capital
use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation
spreading farming across more states of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Intensive agriculture, also known as** intensive farming**, maximizes agricultural production from a given area of land using **higher inputs of labour, machinery, and other farming resources.**
 
• This method represents a stark contrast to **extensive farming**, where the **land is used more broadly with less management or fewer inputs per unit area.**
 
• Intensive agriculture uses practices like **irrigation, advanced fertilizers, and other technological inputs** to **generate a high output per unit of land,** making it well-suited for regions with high population density where land is in short supply.
 
• **The aim** of this agricultural practice is **to grow plentiful crops and raise large numbers of animals cheaply and rapidly,** which often leads to higher environmental impact compared to less intensive farming systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extensive Farming:**

 
 
• Extensive farming is characterized by **low inputs of labour and capital** per unit area of land.
 
• This farming method is traditionally used in **regions with low agricultural productivity, such as remote, mountainous, or dry regions**, where arable land is abundant.
 
• It has** less of an impact on the environment **per unit of area compared to intensive farming, as **it tends not to employ large amounts of harmful fertilizers or pesticides.**
 
• However, it usually **generates less production per unit of land,** which can be a potential downside in areas where the population is growing and food demand is high.
 
 
 
• **Mechanized Farming:**
 
 
• Mechanized farming is characterized by the** use of machinery for various farming operations**, replacing traditional manual and animal labour.
 
• This type of farming is usually employed in developed countries and in places** where the cost of labour is high or labour is scarce.**
 
• Mechanized farming significantly **increases the efficiency and productivity** of the land, making large-scale farming feasible.
 
• On the downside,** it requires significant investment in machinery,** which can be a barrier for small-scale farmers.
 
 
 
• **Diversified Farming:**
 
 
• Diversified farming involves **growing a variety of crops or raising various types of livestock on the same farm** to maximize output and reduce risk.
 
• This type of agriculture **provides a variety of products, promoting food security,** and can help to **safeguard against the failure of a single crop** or livestock.
 
• Diversified farming can be **beneficial to the environment, promoting biodiversity** and reducing the need for chemical inputs as different plants and livestock can help to control pests and replenish soil nutrients.
 
• However, it can** require more labour, knowledge, and management** compared to monocultures due to the complexity of farming multiple crops or livestock types.

questions.question: Nana Sahib, a rebel at Kanpur was the son of which of the following Peshwas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baji Rao ll.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nana Sahib**, born as **Dhondu Pant,** was an Indian Peshwa (prime minister) of the **Maratha empire.**
 
• He was **adopted by Baji Rao II**, who was the **last Peshwa of the Maratha Empire.**
 
• Nana Sahib played a **significant role in the Indian Rebellion of 1857** (also known as the First War of Independence or the Sepoy Mutiny).
 
• He led the revolt in the region of** Kanpur (Cawnpore) **and despite initial successes, **was defeated by British forces **later on.
 
• After the Indian rebellion, he disappeared, and his ultimate fate was never known, leading to various theories and speculations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baji Rao I**:

 
 
• Baji Rao I served as the **seventh Peshwa of the Maratha Empire** from **1720 to 1740**.
 
• Exemplifying Maratha's chivalry and valour, he is** recognized for expanding the Maratha Empire**, especially** in the north**, during his tenure.
 
• Some of Baji Rao's notable achievements include his **victories in the Battle of Palkhed and the Battle of Bhopal.**
 
• Baji Rao I was instrumental in the **spread of Maratha influence** which marked a significant shift in the Indian subcontinent's power dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Balaji Baji Rao:**
 
 
• Also known as** Nana Saheb Peshwa**, Balaji Baji Rao was the **eldest son of Baji Rao I** and served as the **Peshwa of the Maratha Empire from 1740 to 1761.**
 
• His regime in power was marked by territorial expansion via wars and the prosperity of Pune. He made** Pune the effective capital of the Maratha empire** and commissioned several landmark building constructions.
 
• However, his tenure ended tragically with the crushing **Maratha defeat at the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761,** leading to his **death from shock.**
 
 
 
• **Balaji Vishwanath:**
 
 
• Serving as the first of a series of hereditary Peshwas hailing from the **Bhat family,** Balaji Vishwanath held tenure from **1713 to 1720.**
 
• Known for his diplomatic proficiency, he played a key role in **consolidating Maratha power in Maharashtra and beyond.**
 
• He managed to **pacify the Mughal emperor**, thereby gaining crucial legitimacy for the expansionist policies of his Maratha successors.

questions.question:
Match column A with column B. 

 
 

 
 
**Column A (Type of algae)**

 
 
 
**Column B (Proper Name)**

(i)

options.text: a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - i, b - iii, c - ii, d - iv
a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i
a - iii, b - iv, c - ii, d - i

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Blue-green Algae (Cyanobacteria)**

 
 
• Blue-green algae are actually** **bacteria** **and are** also known as Cyanobacteria.**
 
• They are** photosynthetic organisms** and can live in a wide variety of environments,** including freshwater, seawater, damp soil, or rocks.**
 
• Cyanobacteria are known for their significant** contribution to the Earth's oxygen atmosphere.**
 
• They can **exist as single cells** or can form colonies.
 
 
 
• **Red Algae (Rhodophyta)**
 
 
• Red algae, often called **Rhodophyta,** have been identified as one of the oldest groups of **eukaryotic algae.**
 
• They are mostly **found in the warmer waters of the ocean.**
 
• Red algae are of great economic value because of their use in the production of **agar and carrageenan**, substances** used as thickening agents** in various food products.
 
• Their **red colour** is due to the **pigment, phycoerythrin.**
 
 
 
• **Green Algae (Chlamydomonas)**
 
 
• Green algae are a diverse** group of algae **from which plants evolved. Chlamydomonas is a genus of **unicellular green algae.**
 
• Chlamydomonas **species are widely distributed worldwide** and are **found in soil and freshwater.**
 
• They have **two flagella** that allow them to move.
 
• They are known for their green colour due to the **presence of chlorophyll.**
 
 
 
• **Brown Algae (Sargassum)**
 
 
• Brown algae are the most complex type of algae; many are **seaweeds.**
 
• Sargassum is a** brown algae**, known for forming massive floating forests in the ocean.
 
• It is **primarily marine** and is** found in warm-temperate and tropical oceans.**
 
• They provide important **ecological functions** such as providing habitats for a wide variety of marine species.
 
• The **brown colour** is due to the presence of a pigment called **fucoxanthin**, which masks the green colour of chlorophyll.

questions.question: What helps making the acidic food alkaline that is coming from the stomach?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bile juice.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bile juice is secreted by the liver and stored in the gallbladder. It is released into the small intestine when food enters.
 
• Bile neutralizes the acid in chyme, raising its pH and making the intestinal environment more alkaline.
 
• This is a critical step, as the enzymes in the small intestine that further digest food work optimally in an alkaline condition.
 
• Along with neutralizing the acid, bile aids in the emulsification of dietary fat, which helps in its digestion.
 
• It's important to note that excessive bile or reflux of bile into the stomach can cause discomfort and affect the digestive process.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pepsin:
 
 
• Pepsin is an enzyme that is released in the stomach to break down proteins into smaller peptides during digestion.
 
• It is produced by the chief cells in the stomach lining and is activated by the acidic environment of the stomach.
 
• Pepsin is not involved in making food alkaline, instead, it assists in further breaking down food particles.
 
• Faulty regulation or overproduction of pepsin can lead to peptic ulcers or other gastric disorders.
 
 
 
• Gastric Juice:
 
 
• Gastric juice, a combination of pepsin, hydrochloric acid, and other enzymes, is secreted into the stomach to aid in the digestion of food.
 
• It is acidic in nature, with a pH ranging from 1.5 to 3.5, which is essential for pepsin's protein digestion process.
 
• The acidity of gastric juice also kills many bacteria that enter the stomach, providing a protective function against infection.
 
• Gastric juice is not responsible for making food alkaline, but rather for launching the initial stages of digestion in a highly acidic environment.
 
 
 
• Hydrochloric Acid:
 
 
• Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is one of the main components of gastric juice.
 
• It creates the acidic environment in the stomach needed to activate pepsin and other enzymes.
 
• HCl helps to break down food and kill ingested pathogens.
 
• Like pepsin and gastric juice, hydrochloric acid participates in digestion within the stomach, but it does not play a part in making the chyme alkaline.

questions.question: Ashoka sent a mission to spread the principle of Dhamma led by his son, Mahendra and daughter, Sanghamitra to _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ceylon.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Emperor Ashoka sent Buddhist missions **to various places to spread the **principles of Dhamma (Buddhist teachings).**
 
• His son,** Mahendra **(also referred to as Mahinda), and daughter, **Sanghamitra**, were **sent to Ceylon (present-day Sri Lanka)**.
 
• They played a key role in establishing **Theravada Buddhism as the major religion** in the region.
 
• Sanghamitra is** known for carrying a sapling of the sacred Bodhi Tree** under which Buddha achieved enlightenment, **to Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka**.
 
• The tree that grew from the sapling is known as the **Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi** and is one of the **most sacred relics of Buddhists in Sri Lanka.**
 
• As a result of their efforts, Buddhism grew strong roots in Sri Lanka and continues to be the **majority religion there today**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka:**

 
 
• Ashoka, the **third emperor of the Mauryan dynasty,** ruled almost the entire Indian subcontinent from** 268 to 232 BCE**.
 
• He is notably remembered for his conversion to Buddhism following the **Kalinga War in 262-261 BCE**. The war resulted in a vast **loss of life and suffering, which deeply impacted him** and led to his embrace of **Buddhism**.
 
• Post-conversion, Ashoka became known for his principles of **non-violence (ahimsa), love, truth, tolerance, and vegetarianism, which he called "Dhamma" or "Dharma"**.
 
• He attempted to spread these principles throughout his empire, as well as neighbouring states, via envoys and inscriptions on pillars known as the **"Edicts of Ashoka"**.
 
• Ashoka is credited for significant efforts in spreading Buddhism beyond the Indian subcontinent. His son **Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra were sent on a Buddhist mission to Ceylon (current Sri Lanka).**
 
• He also **built and supported numerous stupas** (Buddhist monuments), sponsored the Buddhist council, and played a pivotal role in ordaining monks and nuns.
 
• Ashoka's emblem of the **"Lion Capital" **atop the **Ashoka Pillar at Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh, India,** is adopted as the **National Emblem of India**.

questions.question: Paramvir Chakra, Ashok Chakra and Vir Chakra are presented during the celebration of which day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Republic Day.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Param Vir Chakra, Ashoka Chakra, and Vir Chakra**, which are among **India's highest military honours**, are usually presented during the **Republic Day celebrations.**
 
• Republic Day, which is celebrated on **January 26 every year**, marks the day on which the **Constitution of India came into effect**, establishing India as a republic.
 
• The awards are **presented by the President of India**. It's during the Republic Day parade, that bravery and gallantry awards for military personnel are generally announced.
 
• It's important to note that the **Ashoka Chakra can be awarded to military as well as civilian personnel and can be awarded posthumously.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Independence Day:**

 
 
• Independence Day is celebrated in India on **August 15** every year, marking the **country's independence from British rule in 1947.**
 
• The Prime Minister of India **hoists the Indian flag at the Red Fort in Delhi** and delivers a speech addressing the nation.
 
• The day is marked with various** cultural and patriotic events,** but military awards are not typically presented on this day.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi Jayanti:**
 
 
• Gandhi Jayanti is celebrated on** October 2** each year to **honour the birth of Mahatma Gandhi,** fondly known as the **"Father of the Nation".**
 
• This day is marked by prayer services and tributes across India, including **at Raj Ghat, Mahatma Gandhi's memorial in New Delhi.**
 
• Events like art **exhibitions and essay competitions** are also held, but military awards are not presented on this day.
 
 
 
• **Indian Air Force Day:**
 
 
• Indian Air Force Day is celebrated on **October 8** each year to mark the **foundation of the Air Force in India.**
 
• This day is typically marked by **air displays and parades **at various Air Force Stations in India.
 
• While recognition and awards specific to the air force may be distributed, the highest military honours like the Param Vir Chakra, Ashoka Chakra, and Vir Chakra are not typically presented on this day.

• Malik Kafur was the **slave-general of Alauddin Khilji.**
 
• He led Alauddin Khilji's army in the **battle against Ramachandra of Devagiri.**

questions.question: Padma Shri awardee In 2022, Arjun Singh Dhurve, Is a tribal dancer of which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baiga.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arjun Singh Dhurve**, a tribal artist, was awarded the prestigious** Padma Shri in 2022.**
 
• Dhurve is known for his contribution to the traditional **Baiga dance**.
 
• This dance form **belongs to the Baiga tribe,** an ancient and significant tribe mainly residing in** states like Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, and Odisha.**
 
• The Baiga dance is a folk and tribal dance that carries deep** cultural and traditional significance** for the Baiga tribe.
 
• Arjun Singh Dhurve has made significant **efforts to preserve and promote this traditional dance form**, ensuring its cultural heritage continues to enrich and perpetuate in contemporary society.
 
• The Padma Shri has been accorded to him in** recognition of his invaluable contribution and efforts **towards keeping the traditional art form alive and relevant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhau:**

 
 
• Chhau is a traditional dance form **originating from eastern India**, particularly regions of **Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha.**
 
• It's a unique** fusion of martial arts, folk traditions, and classical Indian dance** elements.
 
• The dance is notable for its** mask use, dramatic representations, and storytelling** through movement.
 
 
 
• **Santhal:**
 
 
• The Santhal dance is a folk dance performed by the **Santhal tribes**, one of the largest tribal communities in India.
 
• Predominantly found in **West Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, Jharkhand and Assam,** the dance is a major part of their cultural identity.
 
• Santhal dance is often performed in large groups and is prominently accompanied by musical instruments like** drums, flutes, and fiddles.**
 
 
 
• **Tertali:**
 
 
• The Tertali dance is a** ritualistic dance** form performed by the** Kamar tribes,** who primarily inhabit areas of **Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• The dance usually involves two or three women sitting on the ground while clanging small metal cymbals (Manjiras) tied to their hands and singing folk tales.
 
• The Tertali dancers often channel unseen forces during their performances, making this dance form a captivating spiritual experience.

questions.question: The number of on-field umpires in cricket matches is _______?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Generally, there are **two on-field umpires** in cricket matches.
 
• One umpire typically **stands behind the stumps at the bowler's end**, which provides a clear view of the bowler's action, the line and length of the delivery, and the batsman's shots.
 
• The second umpire **stands at square leg or a little behind,** allowing them to judge line calls more accurately, such as wides or no-balls due to front foot faults. They can also observe short runs and can assist the main umpire with decisions that require a side-on perspective.
 
• The umpires have the power to make decisions according to the 'Laws of Cricket' regarding all aspects of play, such as fair and unfair play, player conduct, and decisions on whether batsmen are out or not.
 
• In addition to these two on-field umpires, there is also usually a **third (off-field) umpire **and **sometimes a fourth umpire**, who assist the on-field umpires with certain decisions using video replays and other technologies, among other duties.

questions.question: What happens to the atomic size as you go down the group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increases.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The atomic size **increases** as you go down a group in the periodic table.
 
• This increase is due to the addition of** new electron shells** or energy levels.
 
• As more electron shells are added, the outermost electrons are **farther from the nucleus.**
 
• The** increased shielding effect **from inner electrons also **contributes to the larger atomic size.**
 
• This trend of increasing atomic size down a group is** observed across the periodic table's** elements.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1954fb3e7b9568a525e4e2cbbd3e6bfbaeb6381ec1b09f1bc85e023fc1362b66.png]

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties of citizens were added to the Constitution of India, upon the recommendations of which of the following committees?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swaran Singh Committee.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties of citizens were **incorporated** into the Constitution of India.
 
• This addition was based on the recommendations of the** Swaran Singh Committee.**
 
• The committee, chaired by Swaran Singh, was tasked with **studying the feasibility of including Fundamental Duties.**
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976 **introduced these **Fundamental Duties** to the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties emphasize the **responsibilities of citizens towards the nation's integrity, harmony, and progress.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Chelliah Committee:**

 
 
• The Raja Chelliah Committee was** formed in 1991** to suggest** tax reforms in India.**
 
• It focused on **economic and taxation policies**, aiming to improve revenue collection and** promote economic growth.**
 
• Its recommendations led to significant** changes in India's tax structure and policies.**
 
 
 
• **Santhanam Committee:**
 
 
• The Santhanam Committee, officially known as the** Committee on Prevention of Corruption, was established in 1962.**
 
• It aimed to examine measures to **combat corruption in various government departments and organizations.**
 
• The committee's findings and recommendations contributed to the **strengthening of anti-corruption efforts** in India.
 
 
 
• **Kelkar Committee:**
 
 
• The Kelkar Committee, led by **Vijay Kelkar,** has been associated with** multiple economic and financial reforms in India.**
 
• It has provided **recommendations on fiscal policies, taxation, and economic reforms** to boost growth and development.
 
• The committee's reports have** influenced important economic decisions** taken by the Indian government.

questions.question: Who was behind publishing the first News Paper in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Augustus Hickey.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first newspaper in India,** "The Bengal Gazette," **was **established by James Augustus Hickey.**
 
• James Augustus Hickey was **an Irishman** who started the newspaper **in 1780** during the colonial period.
 
• "The Bengal Gazette" is also known as the **Calcutta General Advertiser.**
 
• This newspaper marked a significant milestone in Indian media history, becoming the **pioneer of journalism in the country.**
 
• James Hickey's initiative laid the** foundation **for the development and growth of the press in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deen Bandhu Mitra:**

 
 
• Deen Bandhu Mitra was a **Bengali playwright, poet, and journalist **during the **19th century.**
 
• He is best known for his play** "Nil Darpan," **which highlighted the **oppression faced by indigo farmers under British rule.**
 
• Deen Bandhu Mitra made significant contributions to** Bengali literature and social issues.**
 
 
 
• **Hem Chandrakar:**
 
 
• Hem Chandrakar was an Indian **social worker and a prominent figure **in the tribal and rural development movement.
 
• He worked towards the **welfare and upliftment of tribal communities,** focusing on education and empowerment.
 
• However, Hem Chandrakar was not associated with the publication of the first newspaper in India.
 
 
 
• **Harishchandra Mukherjee:**
 
 
• Harishchandra Mukherjee was an **influential journalist and reformer** in 19th-century India.
 
• He was the editor of** "Hindu Patriot,"** a newspaper that was instrumental in promoting the Indian nationalistic sentiment during the British Raj.
 
• Mukherjee was also heavily involved in **social reform, contributing notably to the cause of widow remarriages in India.**
 
• He was a** supportive voice for the Indian Rebellion of 1857** through his writings in the Hindu Patriot.

questions.question: Which country will host the 2031 ODI Cricket World Cup ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India and Bangladesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2031 Cricket World Cup **will be** co-hosted by India and Bangladesh**.
 
• The decision was **announced by the International Cricket Council (ICC) **confirming the landmark event.
 
• This event is significant as it showcases the collaboration between two major cricketing nations in South Asia.
 
• Cricket is exceedingly **popular in both countries**, and jointly hosting the World Cup symbolizes their strong commitment towards promoting and developing the sport.
 
• It will also be an opportunity for these nations to showcase their unique** culture, hospitality, and the big strides** they have made in infrastructure and facilities necessary to host such a major global sporting event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• International Cricket Council (ICC):

 
 
• The ICC is the global **governing body **for the sport of cricket.
 
• The organization was originally founded as the **'Imperial Cricket Conference' in 1909** by representatives from **Australia, England, and South Africa.** It was renamed to the **'International Cricket Conference' in 1965,** and then took its **current name in 1987.**
 
• The ICC’s main activities include governing cricket internationally, organizing international tours, competitions, and managing the rules, regulations, and equipment for the game.
 
• It is also responsible for the staging of all ICC Events, including the Cricket World Cup, among others.
 
• The ICC presides over the ICC** Code of Conduct, playing conditions, the Decision Review System, and other related matters.**
 
• The **headquarters of the ICC is in Dubai, United Arab Emirates**. It manages all operational matters from Dubai and administrates the game globally.

questions.question: Haryana government announced ______ to provide support to women entrepreneurs, on International Women’s Day 2022.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Matrushakti Udaymita Scheme** was announced to **facilitate women entrepreneurs in Haryana** and to provide them with a supportive ecosystem for business.
 
• The primary aim of this scheme is to create better **opportunities for women in the business sector** and to uplift their socioeconomic status.
 
• This initiative by the Haryana government reflects their **efforts toward gender equality and women's empowerment.**
 
• The announcement was notably made on** International Women's Day 2022, **which emphasizes the significance of the initiative in promoting gender parity.
 
• The Matrushakti Udaymita Scheme is a part of several initiatives being undertaken by various governments in India to encourage female entrepreneurship and to **reduce gender disparity** in the business environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UJJWALA Scheme:**

 
 
• **The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)**, also known as the **UJJWALA Scheme**, is a social welfare program initiated by the Indian Government.
 
• It was launched with the primary objective of providing** clean cooking fuel to poor households in rural and semi-urban areas.**
 
• The scheme supports **providing LPG connections** to families below the poverty line.
 
 
 
• **Mahila E-Haat Scheme:**
 
 
• Mahila E-haat was launched by the** Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India,** to encourage women entrepreneurs and self-help groups (SHGs).
 
• This direct online marketing platform **provides a space for women to showcase their products** across the globe without any charge.
 
• The objective is to strengthen the financial inclusion of women entrepreneurs in the economy by providing a platform where they can market their products worldwide.
 
 
 
• **SWADHAR Scheme:**
 
 
• The SWADHAR Scheme is an effort by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development in India** to uplift and provide a **better life to women in moral danger due to circumstances.**
 
• The scheme provides a supportive institutional framework where women **can be protected and rehabilitated.**
 
• Services provided under this scheme include **food, shelter, counselling, vocational training, and legal aid **to manage their personal and social issues.

questions.question: What is the child sex ratio in India in the 2011 Census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**919 females per 1000 males.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**

__
 
• SSC has given 914 as the correct answer, but according to census 919 is the correct answer. So we have updated the option and answer accordingly. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The** child sex ratio** in India, according to the 2011 Census, was **919females per 1000 males.**
 
• This ratio is a noteworthy demographic indicator that** reflects the societal condition and status of females** in the country.
 
• The ratio is **calculated among children aged 0-6 years, **considered to be a crucial age group due to the particular attention required for their growth and development.
 
• The data from the 2011 census has been utilized in **setting up and implementing various child welfare, gender equality and female empowerment** measures within the country.
 
• **Low sex ratio **in India is a **subject of concern **for policymakers, as it may suggest gender-based discrimination. Therefore, measures are continuously undertaken to improve this scenario.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Census in India:**

 
 
• It was done for the** first time in 1872** under the British **Viceroy Lord Mayo.**
 
• After that, it is conducted at **intervals every 10 years.**
 
• However, the** first complete census of India** was **conducted in 1881.**
 
• **Since 1949**, it is conducted by the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India** under the **Ministry of Home Affairs,** Government of India.
 
• **All censuses after 1951** were conducted under the **1948 Census Act.**
 
• **As of 2011**, the Census of India has been conducted **15 times.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **According to the State Census 2011,**

 
 
• The **most populated state** in India is **Uttar Pradesh** with a population of **19.96 crores.**
 
• The **least populated state** in the country is **Sikkim** with a population of **6,07,688.**
 
• **Mizoram** is the **second least populous state** in India with around **1,091,014 population.**
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh** is the **third least populous state.**
